recommendation: Do not add the 100-bps activation and 25-bps floor to live HYPE yet.
why_now: The first v51 HYPE short crossed 100 bps maximum favorable excursion, making the previously declared mature-floor hypothesis observable on a real forward lifecycle.
evidence_reviewed: The exact v51 HYPE compression baseline with 138 development and four later-confirmation lifecycles.
A fixed-entry causal replay of a100_floor25_only with exact baseline fees, slippage, hourly funding, completed one-minute bars, and gap-through stop references.
The current open HYPE lifecycle's authority-free mature-floor telemetry.
observed_problem_or_opportunity: The native exit can retain large trend winners, but it has no dedicated profit floor. A late floor could reduce large giveback without imposing the previously rejected tight trailing locks.
applicable_market_regime: HYPE compression-breakout entries after a completed-bar path first reaches at least 100 bps favorable excursion.
alternatives_considered: Keep the native opposite-signal, protective-stop, 8-hour review, and 24-hour hard fallback unchanged.
Use the previously rejected 25/40/60-bps activation trailing locks.
Use the 100-bps activation and 25-bps floor-only challenger.
Close on raw indicator opposition rather than a fully eligible opposite intent.
expected_upside: Development sensitivity improved aggregate net return by 33.896500 bps and reduced maximum drawdown by 194.255793 bps across the same 138 entries, but this effect is not independently confirmed.
main_risks_and_failure_modes: The policy originated after observing an unrelated SPCX winner.
Development return excluding the largest winner remained negative under both native and challenger exits.
The four later-confirmation lifecycles produced zero floor triggers, so their unchanged economics do not validate the mechanism.
One-minute OHLC cannot reproduce intrabar event order or every live IOC fill.
A 25-bps gross floor may be near breakeven after entry and exit costs and can gap through the reference.
validation_still_required: Resolve the current predeclared live HYPE activation through its actual native exit and compare the causal floor reference with the realized fill.
Collect at least one independent completed floor trigger and gap/slippage outcome; one trigger is diagnostic, not promotion evidence.
Require positive after-cost effect without the largest winner across a predeclared forward window before proposing live activation.
success_metrics: Independent triggered lifecycles have positive aggregate estimated-minus-native net return after fees, funding, and measured exit slippage.
The improvement remains positive after removing the largest beneficial trigger.
No material increase in stop-wave loss, re-entry interference, or missed opposite-signal exits.
failure_or_rollback_triggers: A forward trigger realizes less than the native exit after costs and the effect remains adverse after additional evidence.
Gap-through execution makes the 25-bps floor nonpositive after costs.
The floor preempts a fully eligible opposite exit or creates inconsistent restart protection.
confidence_level: medium on causal replay arithmetic; low on live economic benefit because confirmation has zero triggers
highest_value_next_investigation: Reconcile the current live HYPE close, including exit reason, signal state, fill, fees, funding, slippage, MFE, giveback, and the counterfactual 100/25 floor.

artifact_status.superseded_reason: v1 mislabeled the challenger's trigger count as a native-control trigger count; economics and deltas were unchanged, but v2 corrects the field.

falsifier: A predeclared independent forward sample with resolved fills and costs shows a robust positive floor effect, including positive leave-largest sensitivity; that would justify an approval-ready live proposal.
